subject: Can estimate abundance and density for small data?

messages.author: c80d4e36e0f796d9
messages.subject: Can estimate abundance and density for small data?
parts:
Dear  colleagues,

Can we estimate abundance and density with small dataset? see attached dataset.

I used to have large dataset before and it all work, but this time only have this small data. 
 I did run it using distance package in R but the estimates of abundance and density doesn't come out and this was stated in the results -  "No survey area information supplied, only estimating detection function". I wonder what is this mean.

> SLdata_hr.simp<-ds (SLdata, truncation = 20, key = "hr", adjustment = "poly")
Starting AIC adjustment term selection.
Fitting hazard-rate key function
AIC= -21.132
Fitting hazard-rate key function with simple polynomial(4) adjustments
AIC= -20.516

Hazard-rate key function selected.
No survey area information supplied, only estimating detection function.

Thanks a lot in advance!
Suzika

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Can estimate abundance and density for small data?
parts:
Suzika

Thanks for your question. The short answer to your question about the warning message: you did not give the appropriate name to the field that specifies the labels for the transects. You need to name the field "Sample.Label" rather than "LineTransect.Label". When doing that, the warning message goes away.

SLdata <- read.csv("E:/troubleshoot/Suzy/Mammal_recce survey.csv")
colnames(SLdata)[3] <- "Sample.Label"

But I think you have more problems than that. Your data indicate you have two strata (AD and CA), but there is only a single transect in each stratum. That is a design that does not permit estimation of variability between transects; it will be difficult to make inference from such a design.

Second, there are only 19 detections in the data set; that will be difficult for detection function fitting. However, those 19 detections are spread among 6 species, further diminishing the number of detections per species (I doubt that deer and squirrels share the same detection function).

Finally, I don't know the units in which effort and perpendicular detection distance is measured, but I suspect there is a problem with the recorded distance measurements. 17 of the 19 detections have recorded detection distance of 0.1, one detection distance of 0.5 and another detection distance of 20. Fitting a detection function will not be possible to data such as that; it does not appear that detectability is a function of distance for those data.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Can estimate abundance and density for small data?
parts:
Dear Eric,

Thank you for your explanation. 

Both AD and CA are transect within an area, meaning only two transect that was exercised within the small area.

The aim of this recce survey was to get an overview of the mammals in that small area near the lake. Thus, unable to carry more replicates due to the presence of Lake. 
Sighting of the squirrels happens to be in the transect.

The perpendicular distance unit is in meters. Most of the detection was from the footprints and dung (for sambar deer, malay badger and civets) while the others was from direct sighting along the transect. 
Yes, when performing the gof, only 2 points were in plot due to no variations in distance records. 

I have a final thought, does the estimation of the density still make sense for this data? as only density estimates result while no abundance estimation. 


Many thanks,

Suzika

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Can estimate abundance and density for small data?
parts:
Suzika

I do not believe density estimation is sensible for these data because of the reasons I posed in my earlier email: a) few detections, b) few replicate transects (inference to a broader area from two transects is unwise) c) virtually no detections at distances other than 0.1, making detection function fitting difficult and d) mixing of data from a dung survey and visual sighting data is unwise.
